$comment: Copy to config/cambridge.json and fill in. The real file is git-ignored
because it holds camera access-authentication credentials.
Read username/password off each body at:

camd.$comment: The C++ daemon. Loopback only by design — nothing outside this Mac talks to it directly.
camd.$comment_ws: WebSocket shares the REST port via HTTP upgrade; one port, one listener.

connection.$comment: Phase 2 lifecycle tuning. A dead camera must never affect the other two.
connection.$comment_backoff: Caps at 15s so a camera that comes back mid-take rejoins fast. The brief's target is reconnect within ~10s of link restore.

cambridge.$comment: The Node app server and web UI. Binds all interfaces so the iPad on the production VLAN can reach it.

logging.$comment: Every state change, timestamped, to a rotating file. This is what we read the morning after something went wrong on a shoot.

atem.$comment: Tally from a Blackmagic ATEM. Read-only — CamBridge never sends the switcher a command. Leave enabled false if there is no switcher.
atem.$comment_mapping: Which ATEM input each camera is plugged into, as numbered on the switcher.

visca.$comment: Accept VISCA so a hardware joystick or controller panel can drive the cameras. Off by default: no reason to have a socket open for hardware that is not there.
visca.$comment_mapping: VISCA address for each camera. Omit the whole mapping to fall back to camera order, which is right for a single-camera setup.

cameras.label: FX3 — Wide
cameras.$comment_fingerprint: Access Authen. Info also shows a fingerprint. Whether the SDK needs it is a Phase 1 open question; record it here once we know.
